target_customer: Developers and companies building realtime web and mobile apps who would pay for support of an open source database
problem: Apps needed live updates pushed from the database rather than polling, which conventional databases did not support.
business_model: Open source database with paid commercial support and hosted offerings

founders.name: Slava Akhmechet
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; later worked at Stripe per press

founders.name: Michael Glukhovsky
founders.background_notes: Former founder per YC page; now product lead at Stripe

exit.reason: Company said it could not build a sustainable business; engineers moved to Stripe and the code was later acquired by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation in February 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: A distributed, sharded database with a custom storage engine, a query language and push based change feeds; the first version was an SSD optimized MySQL engine before the document database.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code meant no licensing lock in and competing document databases had far larger communities; realtime features were the differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Other databases added realtime features over time; RethinkDB shut down in October 2016 and its engineers joined Stripe.

market_need_then: NoSQL databases were rising in 2009 as web apps scaled and developers wanted alternatives to relational stores; the founders initially targeted flash storage and then rethought the database for realtime web apps.

branding.name_origin: A 2015 article ties the name to rethinking the database for apps where data is pushed to clients

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer focused blog and open source voice

branding.brand_signature: Open source realtime database that survived the company
branding.community_and_virality: Over 100 open source contributors per the founder in 2015; community fork RebirthDB in 2018; Stripe matched donations after shutdown

brand_strength.rationale: Strong developer goodwill and community that outlived the company, but market share trailed MongoDB.

pivots.from: SSD optimized storage engine for MySQL
pivots.why: Per a database encyclopedia, the team switched to build a document database like MongoDB; later focus moved to realtime push

outcome_analysis: RethinkDB raised an 8 million Series A in December 2013 after a roughly 1.2 million seed, open sourced the database and grew a strong developer community, but said in October 2016 that it could not build a sustainable business and shut down. Stripe hired the engineers, creditors held the source rights until the Cloud Native Computing Foundation bought them in 2017 and gave the code to the Linux Foundation, so the product lived on without the company.
notes: Directory status is Acquired; the sources show a 2016 shutdown with a team hire by Stripe and a 2017 sale of code rights to the CNCF, so exit type is shutdown. Seed date not found. Total raised conflicts across aggregators (9.2M to 13.3M); about 12M is the most plausible but unverified. Competitor list left empty: no source dated near 2009 named competitors in the search results. Founder backgrounds not found. The rethinkdb.com page now shows version 2.4.4 under community stewardship. Failure factors are my reading of the company's stated lack of a sustainable business model.
